speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me how long you've noticed this breast mass and if it has changed in size or shape recently? Also, have you experienced any nipple discharge, skin changes like dimpling, or fever in this area?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information; given the rapid growth over just four weeks, have you noticed any skin changes like redness, warmth, or "peau d'orange" (an orange peel texture) on that breast? Additionally, is there a palpable lump in the axillary (armpit) region?

REQUEST TEST: Mammogram and Ultrasound of left breast.
REQUEST IMAGES: Left breast imaging studies.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Mammography findings show a smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Biopsy microscopic description reveals leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth. Breast Examination indicates a 6-cm, nontender, multinodular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast with no palpable axillary lymphadenopathy. Vital signs are normal (Temperature 37.0°C, BP 125/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 14 bpm). Inspection shows no skin changes, nipple retraction, or discharge.
